title: Telemetry graft latency wave — incident review and runbook draft
content:
Executive summary:

On 2029-08-20 at ~14:32 UTC a sustained latency wave affected the Hosted API streaming path for ~26 minutes, causing 95th/99th p99 token latencies to spike by 3–6x and increasing client-observed stream reconnections. Impact: user-facing latency degradation and a small but noticeable rise in 5xxs for streaming sessions. This document captures the timeline, root cause analysis (RCAs), immediate mitigations, and a proposed runbook patch to reduce blast radius for future telemetry graft events.

High-level impact:
- Window: 14:32–14:58 UTC
- Affected surface: Hosted API — streaming responses (chunked SSE / multiplexed gRPC streams)
- Symptom: progressive token latency increase across regions; clients reported stalls then reconnects; ~0.9% increase in streaming 5xx during the window (from baseline 0.08% to 0.98%)
- Customer-visible impact: delayed tokens, truncated streams requiring client reconnects for ~3% of active streaming sessions during spike

Short description of root cause (TL;DR):
A debug telemetry graft — introduced to collect high-cardinality prefix histogram samples —was rolled out to the streaming edge path without sufficient sampling throttles. The graft code added a blocking path that performed synchronous KV cache lookups and histogram serialization on the streaming thread for a subset of requests. Under typical load the additional work amplified tail latency and produced head-of-line stalls inside the streaming multiplexer, cascading to token generation stalls and client reconnect behavior.

Timeline (reconstructed from traces, logs, and oncall notes):
- 14:29 UTC: Canary metrics for telemetry graft show slight CI smoke but within thresholds. No rollout guard trip.
- 14:32 UTC: Monitoring alerts fire: streaming p99 token latency > 4x over baseline in region us-west-2. Pager duty engaged (oncall: Evan P).
- 14:34 UTC: SRE initial triage: high p99 observed across multiple edge cells; CPU and GPU utilization normal; network error traces rare.
- 14:36 UTC: Traces show large tailed request durations in the streaming multiplexer; execution snapshots show blocking KV lookups called from streaming worker pool.
- 14:40 UTC: Engineering confirms recent telemetry graft rollout (rollout id: graft-2029-08-20-12) touched streaming-path instrumentation.
- 14:45 UTC: Temporary mitigations applied: rate-limit telemetry sampling at the edge via config flag (telemetry.sample.rate=0.01) and disable sync histogram serialization (telemetry.histogram.sync=false) in the edge cluster.
- 14:52 UTC: Latency begins to drop; token p99 returns to within 20% of baseline.
- 14:58 UTC: All rolling mitigations in place and cluster metrics stable. Post-incident monitoring window established for 2 hours.

Detailed root cause analysis:
1) Code path change: graft-2029-08-20-12 added a telemetry collector that records per-request prefix histograms and immediately writes them to persistent KV (for interactive debugging). The implementation used a synchronous write on the same thread responsible for streaming serialization.

2) Design issue: The telemetry graft assumed that writes would be fast (microseconds) and didn't consider the distribution of prefix cardinality (hot prefixes produce much heavier histogram objects). Several requests produced histograms with 100–1000s of buckets requiring non-trivial serialization time (milliseconds), blocking the streaming worker.

3) Sampling/guard failure: Rollout was performed with a sampling rate of 10% (telemetry.sample.rate=0.1) and no backpressure controls. Under steady-state request mix the additional work multiplied tail latency on the streaming multiplexer.

4) Observability blindspot: No specific SLO or alerting existed for telemetry collector blocking time (we only alerted on end-to-end token latency and streaming 5xx count). By the time token latency alert fired, internal streaming worker queues were already backed up.

Contributing factors:
- Recent change merged from infra PR #2981 added telemetry graft to streaming edge to diagnose prefix drift; code review missed sync-call performance hazard.
- Canary validation was limited to QPS/CPU checks, not tail latency or micro-profile tracing of the streaming worker. Canary thresholds were too permissive.
- The streaming path uses a small bounded worker pool for serialization; blocked workers create head-of-line stalls.
- SRE alerting didn't include a metric for "streaming worker blocking time" nor "histogram serialize duration".

Immediate mitigations and why they worked:
- Reduced sample rate from 10% -> 1% (telemetry.sample.rate=0.01): fewer graft events reduced the probability of encountering hot prefixes concurrently, decreasing blocking pressure.
- Disabled synchronous histogram serialization (telemetry.histogram.sync=false) and switched to enqueuing histogram writes to an asynchronous buffer worker. This returned streaming workers to non-blocking execution paths.
- Rolled mitigation config via remote config with rapid rollback window; mitigations were low-risk config flips and required no full deploy.

Metrics inspected during the incident:
- token_latency_p99 by region (graph referenced in linked_artifacts)
- streaming_worker_queue_length per edge cell
- telemetry_histogram_serialize_duration_ms (derived from spans)
- streaming_5xx_rate and reconnect_count

Runbook changes (draft):
1) Add a new SLO/alert: streaming_worker_block_time > 10ms for > 5 min -> page SRE primary and notify infra owners.
2) Add micro-profiling checks to canaries: any deploy that touches streaming path must run a tail-latency microbenchmark (10k synthetic streaming requests with hot-prefix distribution) and fail the canary if p99 increases by >25% relative to baseline.
3) Telemetry graft rules: any telemetry that serializes data synchronously on request threads must be gated behind an async buffer or background writer. New code review checklist item: "no sync IO on streaming worker threads".
4) Sampling safe defaults: telemetry.sample.rate default must be 0.01 unless explicit justification and SLA sign-off from infra and SRE.
5) Feature-flag gating: rollout of high-cardinality telemetry must default to off; staged rollouts require alpha->beta->canary->global steps with manual signoff at each step.

Proposed long-term fixes (owners and ETA):
- Infra: implement a lightweight in-process async histogram buffer with backpressure and per-prefix spill-to-file policy (owner: Omar A, ETA: 4w)
- SRE: add streaming_worker_block_time metric and dashboard; integrate into alerting (owner: Maya C, ETA: 2w)
- Developer experience: update deploy gating to require micro-latency bench for streaming-path changes (owner: Lina R, ETA: 3w)
- Codebase: revert or rework graft-2029-08-20-12 to asynchronous path and per-prefix size cap (owner: PR author Evan P, ETA: 1w for hotfix branch, 3w for full rework)

Communication notes (who was notified and when):
- Customers with SLOs impacted (~12 customers with dedicated monitors) were notified via status.redwood at 14:49 UTC with "reducing latency, mitigation in progress". Follow-up detailed incident email to affected account contacts scheduled for 2029-08-21 09:00 PDT.
- Internal slack channel #sre-incident-4129 used for triage. Engineering postmortem thread created in #eng-postmortems.

Open questions / unresolved items:
- Why did canary validation not catch the tail effect? Action: get full canary logs and compare microbench harness outputs (owner: Lina R).
- Are there other instrumentation grafts with similar sync characteristics deployed recently? Quick grep + audit needed (owner: Priya S).
- Exact distribution of prefix cardinality in production: need analytics export to estimate worst-case serialization sizes (owner: Evan P).

Immediate action items (owners and deadlines):
- Hotfix PR to change graft to async for streaming path and cap histogram size (Evan P, due 2029-08-23).
- Add streaming_worker_block_time metric and brief dashboard (Maya C, due 2029-09-04).
- Run canary microbenchmark for latest infra PRs touching streaming path (Lina R, due 2029-08-26).
- Audit telemetry-related PRs merged in last 30 days for any sync IO (Priya S, due 2029-08-28).

Runbook draft snippets (to add to the main SRE runbook under "Streaming latency spikes"):
- Detection flow:
  1) Alert: streaming token p99 > threshold -> check streaming_worker_block_time metric and worker queue length
  2) If worker_block_time elevated: query traces for spans with "telemetry.histogram.serialize" or "graft-kv-write" tags
  3) If traces show sync writes on streaming threads: flip remote config telemetry.histogram.sync=false and reduce sample rate to 0.01

- Mitigation play (if remote config not available):
  1) Isolate affected edge cells by draining new streaming sessions to other cells
  2) Temporarily scale streaming worker pool (careful: scaling increases memory pressure; only as last resort)
  3) Coordinate with infra team to toggle canary flag for graft rollout to off

Post-incident follow-ups & verification plan:
- Verify hotfix PR resolves microbench anomalies by running the 10k synthetic streaming test with worst-case prefixes (Evan P, post-merge verification).
- Monitor production for 48 hours, specifically token_latency_p99, streaming_worker_block_time, streaming_5xx_rate, reconnect_count.
- Run a red-team exercise: introduce a synthetic high-cardinality prefix workload in staging to validate backpressure and async buffer behavior (owner: SRE ops, due 2029-09-15).

Lessons learned (short):
- High-cardinality telemetry can be a production hazard if implemented synchronously on hot code paths.
- Canary validation must include tail-latency microbenching for streaming / low-latency code paths.
- Observability must include micro-metrics (worker-block time) in addition to high-level SLOs.

Appendix (artifacts & logs):
- Sample trace id: trace-0a7b9c (see linked_artifacts for full traces)
- SRE incident channel: #sre-incident-4129 (Slack log pinned to confluence linked_artifacts)
- Deploy diff: github.com/redwood-inference/infra/compare/graft-2029-08-20-12

Notes to reviewers (quick):
- This doc is an operational draft: please add missing links to charts you used during triage and call out if additional owners should be assigned.
- We should schedule a 1hr post-incident review with infra + SRE + graft author next week; propose 2029-08-28 16:00 UTC.

Raw on-call snippets (copied from slack for fidelity):
- Evan P @14:33: "token p99 climbing fast in us-west-2; traces show long sync write spans from streaming-worker-17"
- Omar A @14:37: "confirmed new telemetry graft deployed this morning, rolling config id graft-2029-08-20-12"
- Priya S @14:42: "flipped telemetry.histogram.sync=false in edge remote-config; dropping sample rate to 0.01"
- Maya C @14:50: "p99 trending down; continuing to watch for reconnects"

End of document.
